shortcut_name: collapse the voltage rule to proper 3-coloring
evidence: "colors = [0] * n  # 0 = uncolored, 1,2,3 = colors"; "domain bitmask: bit 0->color1, bit1->color2, bit2->color3"; qwen's special case assigns all vertices voltage 1 when "m == 0"
affordance_in_statement: The voltage assignment must satisfy a specific rule: the sum of the voltages assigned to the two connected components must not equal twice the voltage of either of the two components.
removal_suggestion: Present the same constraint as an explicit allowed-pair relation, listing only the unordered pairs {1,2}, {1,3}, and {2,3}, rather than stating the algebraic midpoint condition. This preserves the task but prevents solutions hardcoded around the immediately recognized inequality from applying unchanged.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats voltages as three graph colors and searches with an MRV/colored-neighbor heuristic.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The rule forbids equal endpoint voltages, so every link is a standard inequality constraint.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses three finite color domains with propagation and degree-based ordering.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The rule reduces every edge to a binary constraint between values in {1,2,3}.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses ordinary graph-coloring backtracking and recognizes the empty-edge case as trivially colorable.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The link condition is equivalent to requiring different colors at the two endpoints.

common_affordance: All survivors exploit the algebraic rule's equivalence to proper 3-coloring: a connected pair may not receive the same voltage.
recommended_edit: Replace the midpoint-equation wording with an explicit permitted-pair table for linked components: the two voltages must be one of {1,2}, {1,3}, or {2,3}. Keep the same examples and I/O, but require solvers to process the relation rather than assuming a hardcoded inequality.
